obligations.statement: Given one valid instance of each public contract kind, each instance is accepted unchanged.
Given an internal inventory object that is not one of the five public contracts, root contract validation rejects it.
Given a result whose execution did not complete but whose logical outcome claims satisfied or violated, validation rejects it.
Given a plan task with a missing required field, an unknown field, or a wrongly typed field, validation rejects it.

Given a structured boundary value whose `contractVersion` is not `quire-verification/e02-draft-2`, including the former draft-1 value, validation rejects it without compatibility inference or fallback.
The exported contract version equals the schema contract-version constant.
The exported input, applicability, readiness, execution-status, and logical-outcome vocabularies equal their schema definitions.
Duplicate plan task IDs, unknown dependency IDs, and dependency cycles are rejected by explicit cross-record validation.
Generated E02 input types resolve their shared artifact envelopes from the retained shared-reference schema; no independently authored E02 copy of the shared artifact-reference field set exists.
The four retained JSON fixtures and every embedded or adapted public contract instance pass the authoritative schema.
A newly discovered JSON fixture without a registered handler fails validation and names the file.
Fixture validation executes as a distinct CI step before the unit-test suite.
Every unique method preserves its identifier, name, class, definition, evidence kind, applicability, tooling hints, and source module.
Duplicate definitions or unreadable roots preserve the diagnostic first-wins view but mark the adapted registry unqualified.
Positive advice maps to applicable selections with reasons, while empty inconclusive advice maps to unknown residual applicability.
State, relational, trace, fault, and manual properties retain their distinct required input shapes.

An applicable selection with a qualified compatible `native-producer` capability, all required prerequisites, and an in-limit selected budget emits a ready invocable verification task; other ready work remains non-invocable unless a requirement defines a separate invocation boundary.
Missing capability support emits an unsupported non-invocable verification task with an actionable gap.
Missing bindings, tools, permissions, qualification, reviewer assignment, or policy freshness emit blocked work and explicit prerequisite tasks.
A fault task lacks invocation permission until non-production authorization, injection binding, and independent observation binding are present.
Multiple compatible capabilities without an explicit capability selection fail planning as ambiguous.

A difference in any required technique, property, subject, profile, binding, dependency, execution scope, plan, task, run, producer, or adapter dimension prevents a match and names the differing dimension.
No exact candidate yields missing status while retaining every nearby candidate's scope-mismatch diagnostics.
More than one exact candidate yields ambiguous status with deterministically ordered candidate result IDs.
Duplicate result IDs or obligations lacking a technique and task-level result binding are rejected.
A result beyond its explicit validity or obligation maximum age is classified stale before its logical outcome determines status.
Unsupported, failed, incomplete, untriggered, observation-inadequate, partial, assumption-unmet, violated, and supported cases remain distinguishable.
Simultaneous partial participation, unmet assumption, and logical violation emit all three gap kinds.
The assessment denominator and output contain one entry for every inventoried obligation, including obligations without results.
Provenance and native artifact references remain present in the assessment view.
The assessment identifies Quoin as evidence owner and records that no sufficiency decision was made.
Objects with identical JSON meaning and different property insertion order canonicalize equally and produce the same digest.
RFC 8785 number formatting and UTF-16 property ordering match the canonicalization library behavior.

Malformed JSON bytes, ill-formed Unicode escapes, and attempted serialization of non-finite numbers are rejected before hashing or comparison; Rust types make undefined values, sparse arrays, cyclic values, and non-JSON objects unrepresentable at this boundary.
Every produced digest carries the `sha256-jcs:` domain prefix.
Catalog parity compares complete method records keyed by `techniqueId`, independent of source array order.
Reversing or rotating unique catalog methods leaves adapted technique output unchanged.
A parity mismatch returns a completed result with logical outcome violated and an assessed violated obligation.
An adapter exception returns failed results with logical outcome not-evaluated and assessed failed obligations.
The manual inspection result remains not-run until a verification owner supplies a disposition.
The report's claim limit states that no external method, parser, fault, or human review is claimed.
Applicable, not-applicable, and unknown selections retain their exact applicability while capability availability changes readiness independently.
A stale policy or unavailable capability cannot produce an invocable task even when advice reports the technique as applicable.
An authored property classification is preserved exactly, and an omitted classification is emitted as `unknown`.
An empty property classification is rejected rather than emitted as authored or treated as unknown.
Required, recommended, and optional policy priorities and non-empty explanations validate, and task priority and reasons equal their authored selection values.
A selection-policy rule containing a `score` is rejected instead of being treated as an authored priority.
Each distinct missing required prerequisite emits exactly one plan-level setup task, and each affected verification task depends on its setup-task identifier.

Required verification work remains present and non-invocable when a capability-declared resource allocation or the selected finite native-execution budget is absent; the planner emits one deterministic resource-allocation setup task for each exact missing allocation identity.
A prerequisite is satisfied only by an exact kind-and-identifier match; caller input cannot mark an expired selection policy current.

A setup task carries its exact prerequisite and a sorted nonempty `requiredBy` list of verification-task identifiers; it carries no property input and does not invent a property or technique identity for plan-level work.
Every composite setup-task and verification-task identifier injectively encodes its component values, including values containing the identifier delimiter.

An applicable ready task with one qualified `native-producer` capability and an in-limit budget receives a closed runner request whose capability ID, adapter ID/version, permissions, selected budget, native artifact interface, and complete role-specific input are exact JCS copies of the selected records; descriptive catalog text cannot create a capability or field.

A non-applicable, unknown, blocked, unsupported, stale, unqualified, manual, budget-absent, or over-limit task has a null runner request and `invocationAllowed: false`; absent budget adds one deterministic resource-allocation setup dependency, while an over-limit budget retains both requested and limiting values in a `budget-exceeded` gap.
A fault runner request remains null until non-production authorization, injection binding, and an independent observation binding are all exactly present.

The plan names Quoin as evidence owner and leaves sufficiency to an authored human decision; the closed runner request contains no evidence store, logical outcome, or automated sufficiency decision, and its selected wall-clock budget is at most NFR-006's ten-second execution ceiling.

State input requires a validated artifact envelope whose value kind is `snapshot` plus a nonempty property expression; relational input requires distinct nonempty left and right subject identities plus a nonempty relation.

Trace input requires a validated artifact envelope whose value kind is `trace`, a nonempty clock profile, and a nonempty completion statement; fault input requires validated `fault-model` and `oracle` artifact envelopes plus a nonempty requested injection site.

Manual property input requires a validated artifact envelope whose value kind is `review-procedure` and a duplicate-free nonempty array drawn only from `accept`, `revise`, and `reject`; the planner preserves the authored array order, emits a null native runner request, and keeps `invocationAllowed` false even when its human prerequisites are present.

The planner matches embedded envelopes to opaque strict-reader outputs by exact JCS equality and role; a missing field, equal relational subject identities, wrong reference version or role, envelope absent from those outputs, cross-variant field, duplicate disposition, or unexpected field refuses before plan emission instead of being ignored or guessed.
One parser-portfolio request retains complementary state/property, relational/differential, and manual-review tasks with separate prerequisites and runner eligibility.
A byte reference is accepted only when its version, kind, authority, identity, structured revision, exact byte digest, and wire identity/version are supported and match locally supplied bytes.

A semantic reference is accepted only when its byte artifact, language, semantic-profile definition digest, duplicate-free required-feature set, and selected canonical identity are supported and internally consistent; a null semantic profile requires null language and canonical identity plus an empty feature set.

Before materializing a JSON object, duplicate decoded member names, including escape-equivalent spellings, refuse as `invalid_wire`; unknown versions or required features, wrong role kinds, digest mismatch, stale references, identity-content conflict, malformed source correspondence, and ambiguous equivalence refuse with their corresponding stable code before planning or result matching.
Reordered required features compare as the same set, while every other collection follows its owning contract's declared ordering or identity-key rule.

The reader accepts only the selected `quire.verification.jcs` / `rfc8785-v1` / `sha256` canonical identity and exact `trace`, `fault-model`, `review-procedure`, `oracle`, `observation`, and `review-disposition` roles without placing `sha256-jcs:` semantic digests in `sha256:` byte-digest fields.

Version 2 accepts only artifact/semantic envelopes with `ix.artifact-ref/3-draft`; retained version 1 accepts only source-map/migration envelopes under its exact schema. Draft-1 artifact/semantic evidence is not reinterpreted as current, no migration is inferred, and no fallback reader treats an unknown kind or version as supported.

The independent consumer verifies a repository-retained digest manifest for the exact amendment schema, all fourteen amendment fixture files, and the retained version-1 schema; executes every upstream and B-authored positive/adverse case without producer code or network schema retrieval; and reports snapshot drift before reference interpretation.

Every TechniqueResult carries an `oracleContributions` array of closed contribution objects. A `satisfied` or `violated` logical outcome requires at least one contribution; other outcomes may carry an empty array. Each contribution requires nonempty `contributionId`, exact `oracleRef` and `observationRef` envelopes, and `relation`. `shared` requires only a nonempty `dependenceGroupId`; `derived` requires only a closed exact `derivedFrom` pair of `resultId` and `contributionId`; `independent` and `unknown` admit neither conditional field.

Before result matching or classification, the assessor requires every contribution envelope to match an opaque strict-reader output by exact JCS equality and exact `oracle` or `observation` role. Duplicate opaque validation values are idempotent. A missing validation output, wrong role, unsupported version, changed reference dimension, or extra contribution field refuses with the existing schema/shared-reference error rather than entering the dependence graph.

Contribution IDs are unique within each result. Every derived pair resolves to exactly one other supplied contribution, is not a self-reference, and the directed derived graph is acyclic. Duplicate IDs refuse as `duplicate_oracle_contribution_id`; absent, self, or cyclic sources refuse as `invalid_oracle_lineage` before any assessment is returned.

Distinct technique or result identifiers do not establish independence. Contributions from uniquely selected results connected by an exact shared oracle, observation, declared group, or derived pair emit exactly one closed `correlated-oracle` finding per connected component, with at least two lexically sorted closed `(resultId, contributionId)` members and unique lexically sorted bases that name every edge basis present in that component. Ambiguous candidates do not enter the graph, and one result selected for multiple obligations contributes each member once.

Relation `unknown`, a `shared` group represented by only one selected member, or a valid derived source outside the selected-result graph emits one closed `oracle-dependence-unknown` finding with the corresponding declared reason and makes no independence claim.

Permuting result, obligation, contribution, or opaque-validation input order cannot change the JCS assessment. Each selected result's complete contributions are retained separately in contribution-ID order, the always-present dependence-finding array is JCS-sorted, and structurally duplicate findings are emitted once.

The assessment preserves each obligation and contribution separately, emits no numeric method score or aggregate assurance level, identifies Quoin as evidence owner, and records sufficiency as `not-made`.
The effective expiry is the earlier of result `validUntil` and result `producedAt` plus obligation `maxAgeSeconds`; the result is stale only when assessment time is later than that expiry.
Assessment exactly at the effective expiry remains fresh, and one nanosecond after the expiry is stale; equivalent RFC 3339 offsets yield the same classification.
A result with `producedAt` later than assessment time or `validUntil` earlier than `producedAt` is refused with stable code `invalid_temporal_order`.

An invalid timestamp, a missing obligation maximum age, a maximum age outside `0..=9007199254740991` seconds, or checked expiry arithmetic outside the RFC 3339 timestamp domain is refused before result classification.

A stale classification takes precedence over the compatibility summary while preserving every applicable execution, logical, activation, participation, assumption, adequacy, provenance, and native-artifact field and finding.
The valid-source baseline contains completed, satisfied, fully participating direct-parse and parse-format-reparse results from the exact native candidate.

A single declared syntax mutation yields its exact expected diagnostic code and source location as a completed, violated result, while an unexpected process or protocol failure remains failed and not-evaluated.
Removing one required runner, binding, tool, or resource prerequisite leaves the affected task blocked, emits actionable setup work, and creates no fabricated execution result.

Assessing an otherwise exact result after its earliest freshness bound reports stale and retains its logical, participation, assumption, adequacy, provenance, native-artifact, and dependence findings.
Reused or unknown oracle and observation relationships remain explicit correlation findings; technique count does not imply independence or an aggregate score.
The manual task remains separate from both native techniques, carries its exact review procedure and allowed dispositions, and cannot be passed to the native runner.
Setup and binding observations are stored in a phase distinct from every incremental method and complete-run observation.

The series contains exactly one setup observation at repetition zero and one direct-parse, parse-format-reparse, and complete-run observation for each repetition one through five, retaining all 16 raw valid or invalid observations in collection order with exact candidate and environment identity.
Invalid, interrupted, or identity-mismatched observations retain a reason, do not become zero-duration samples, and do not enter numeric summaries.
Each phase summary reports only its valid sample count, minimum, median, and maximum in integer nanoseconds using the documented deterministic calculation.
Recomputing summaries from the retained raw observations produces the report values exactly.
The report states the measurement population, exclusions, clock, command order, cache treatment, environmental differences, uncertainty, and plausible alternative explanations.
The report limits interpretation to this candidate and fixture and makes no ROI, delivery, throughput, scale, broad-effectiveness, certification, or sufficiency claim.
A negative, fractional, or larger-than-9007199254740991 duration is retained as invalid with its reason and never enters a numeric summary.
An empty or duplicate observation ID, duplicate or missing phase/repetition pair, repetition outside zero through five, or reordered prescribed series refuses with `invalid_measurement_series`.
One closed internal schema definition validates the VP04 report envelope without admitting it as a sixth public contract or duplicating its Rust shape by hand.

The sealed core has a nonempty report ID and contains the exact candidate, subject, mutation, commands, dependency closure, environment, plan, tasks, runs, producers, adapters, assessment time, uniquely identified raw effort observations, interpretation, and claim limits needed to reproduce the automated evidence.

The core digest excludes the disposition, and one verified disposition artifact refers to that digest with a unique nonempty disposition ID, exact reviewer and procedure identity, observation time, and value `accept`, `revise`, or `reject`.
An absent disposition leaves the report incomplete; duplicate, foreign, unsupported, digest-invalid, or procedure-invalid dispositions refuse with the corresponding stable code.

Finalization preserves every automated result and measurement unchanged, identifies Quoin as evidence owner, records sufficiency as `not-made`, and makes no claim that supplied reviewer provenance is cryptographically authenticated.
Every tested JSON property-order and catalog-order permutation produces identical canonical or adapted output.
Exact-match candidates and independent result gaps appear in deterministic identifier or canonical order.
Runtime contract validators and exported vocabularies derive from the single versioned JSON Schema packet.
Every discovered direct-child JSON fixture executes a registered schema-validation handler.
The E02 schema and generated runtime resolve shared artifact envelopes from the exact retained shared-reference schema instead of restating its fields.
Every tested adverse, ambiguous, unqualified, or pending state remains distinct from supported evidence.
Bounded reports retain explicit claim limits and make no automated sufficiency decision.
Governed executable paths contain no JavaScript or TypeScript source files.
Formatting, Clippy with denied warnings, the complete Rust test suite, and dependency policy checks all exit successfully.

Every Rust test used as acceptance evidence imports `ix_trace_rs::trace` and carries a compiler-checked bare `#[trace(...)]` marker whose TC and acceptance-criterion arguments are each discovered and bound by `quire coverage --scope . --json`; compiler acceptance alone is insufficient.
A clean CI runner resolves the exact reviewed `ix-trace-rs` source from a repository-contained snapshot with recorded upstream revision and no cross-repository credential.

`AGENTS.md` names the available Cargo build/test gate, and `LICENSE-DECISION.md` identifies `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` plus `docs/artifact-rights.md` as the current dependency and rights records without claiming that a removed npm manifest or JavaScript dependency is current.
A public ingestion path rejects a serialized JSON document larger than 16 MiB before deserialization.
Contract validation rejects a JSON value nested deeper than 128 levels.
Contract validation rejects any JSON array containing more than 100,000 items.
The executor invokes an exact absolute executable with a separate argument vector, no shell, a fresh run directory, and only explicitly declared environment entries.
A request accepts a positive declared deadline no greater than 10 seconds and refuses an absent, zero, negative, non-finite, or larger deadline with `invalid_execution_deadline` before child launch.

A process group still live at its accepted declared deadline is signaled, the direct child is reaped, and group disappearance is observed before returning `execution_timeout`; failure to send the signal or observe disappearance returns `process_containment_failure` with trigger `execution_timeout` and never claims the group terminated. Neither result carries a logical outcome claim.

Standard output or error is accepted through exactly 16 MiB; the first excess byte signals the process group, reaps the direct child, and returns `output_limit_exceeded` with the stream name, count, and limit but not the excess bytes only after group disappearance is observed. Failed signaling or observation returns `process_containment_failure` with trigger `output_limit_exceeded`.

A signal, unexpected exit code, invalid UTF-8, malformed method response, or descendant surviving the direct child returns a distinct typed failed result without panic, unreported containment failure, partial success, or logical outcome claim.

A candidate path that is relative, outside the selected execution root, absent, non-regular, or resolves through a symbolic link is refused before child launch; lack of the selected Linux descriptor/process-group profile refuses with `unsupported_execution_profile`.

The executor opens the root and root-relative candidate with `openat2` using `RESOLVE_BENEATH`, `RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS`, and `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS`, retains the admitted descriptor through launch, and invokes only its trusted descriptor-backed `/proc/self/fd` path; replacing the request pathname after admission cannot substitute the executed bytes.

After requesting group termination, the executor reaps the direct child before waiting at most one second for process-group disappearance; it reports `process_group_terminated: true` only after observing disappearance, and otherwise returns `process_containment_failure` with the original failure code retained as `trigger`.

metrics.name: coverage.backed
metrics.method: rows of the declared reference tables whose trace target is bound by at least one source symbol; `matched` counts the evidence symbols that bound a trace id out of the `examined` evidence symbols walked, so matched 0 of a non-zero examined is a ratio computed over a corpus the binder could not read

metrics.name: authoring.tag_rate
metrics.method: evidence symbols whose attached annotation block carries an id-shaped token, whether or not the declared trace grammar can read it; `value` counts tagged symbols, while `matched` counts candidates classified as tagged or untagged so an honest zero is not mistaken for an unread population

metrics.name: coverage.self_named_binding.rust
metrics.method: evidence symbols carrying a separator-delimited id in their own declaration name whose id was read by a declared name form; comment and attribute bindings do not satisfy this premise

metrics.name: coverage.property_shaped
metrics.method: criteria the FR-052 classifier reads a property shape from; `matched` counts criteria that reached the classifier at all

metrics.name: coverage.specific_shaped
metrics.method: extractable criteria whose shape names what property to write — every shape but the `universal` catch-all, `example` and `unclassified`; `matched` counts criteria that reached the classifier. NOT a quality ranking: a `universal` criterion is often the right thing to write

metrics.name: coverage.no_symbol_rows
metrics.method: unbacked rows whose declared test type is in the module's `no_source_symbol` vocabulary, counted over every row reconciled

metrics.name: coverage.implements
metrics.method: production symbols carrying at least one declared `implements` marker, counted over the production symbols examined; a zero means none is annotated, not that none was read

metrics.name: minting.section_hit_rate
metrics.method: documents whose declared `section:` heading was found, over the documents a required trace target's `archetype:` selected and its `exclude:` kept, plus documents where an optional target's section was present; counted per (trace target, document) pair. An optional absent section is outside the population. A required miss reads the archetype right and the heading wrong, so the whole table is stranded and its ids never enter `coverage.backed`'s denominator at all
